why: Flipping every significant bit is XOR with a mask of all ones that is exactly as wide as the number: base10 ^ ((1 << bit_length) - 1).
hints: XOR with 1 flips a bit, XOR with 0 keeps it. Which mask flips exactly the significant bits?
The mask is 2^L - 1 where L is the number of bits up to and including the highest 1.
Compute L with bit_length (or by shifting right until zero), build the mask, XOR. O(log n).
pitfalls: Do not use ~base10: it flips all 32 (or infinitely many in Python) bits and gives a negative number.
Leading zeros above the highest 1 must stay zero, so 30 (11110) becomes 1, not a large number.
